items.title: Hyundai Made the Elantra Cool Because It Thinks Sedans Are Worth Investing In
items.summary:
Sedans have been on the ropes for a long time, but they haven’t been knocked out yet. The easiest path is to stretch the lifespan of existing models, maintaining a presence in the relevant segments without spending big. That’s not what Hyundai is doing. The compact Elantra just got a dramatic redesign with complex and precisely fitted body panels that will likely be as expensive to produce as they were to engineer. That’s because Hyundai knows that SUVs aren’t always the answer.

America “loves SUVs,” but increased emphasis on affordability has a lot of customers taking a second look at sedans, Hyundai Motor North America Senior Vice President of Product Planning Olabisi Boyle told The Drive in an interview at the 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show.

Hyundai 

“What we found is, in the last year, especially with the emphasis on affordability, there are other people who are just like, ‘I’ll move to a sedan,'” Boyle said, adding that other brands have seen sedan sales increase almost to the levels of comparable SUVs. And that’s why Hyundai can justify spending the money to turn the humble Elantra into a retro-futuristic fever dream.

When asked if sedans are worth investing in, Boyle responded, “Yes, they have been for us, and they will consistently be. There will always be a market for it. I just think at least in the near term, not as much as SUVs.”

Don’t confuse this with Hyundai going all-in on sedans. The automaker is diving into body-on-frame pickups and SUVs , and with the discontinuation of the non-N version of the Ioniq 6 , it only has two mass-market sedans in its U.S.…
items.t: Hyundai Made the Elantra Cool Because It Thinks Sedans Are Worth Investing In

items.title: I’m Legally Obligated to Tell You That a BMW Z1 Is for Sale
items.summary:
There’s no shortage of great BMWs to own, but if you want to really stand out, things get a little harder. Yes, the E46 M3 and E39 M5 are among the best driver’s cars ever made, but every enthusiast knows that and so you’re bound to see them at Cars and Coffee. If you never want that to have a chance of happening, and are at least a little adventurous, something delightfully obscure has popped up for sale.

Currently listed on eBay (via Barn Finds ) with a buy-it-now price of $68,995, it’s a 1991 BMW Z1 done up as a tribute to the handful of these cars tuned by Alpina back in the day. Just 66 of those were built, designated RLE (Roadster Limited Edition), out of about 8,000 total Z1s built over the car’s short production run, which started a BMW roadster lineage that only recently ended with the Z4 . The Z1 was not sold in the United States when new, but this car is now legal under the 25-year rule.

Credit: Dusty Cars via eBay 

Unveiled at the 1987 Frankfurt Motor Show and launched into production the following year, the Z1 was a technological showcase for BMW. It featured Xenoy thermoplastic body panels, as well as the Z-axle multilink rear suspension that would become a common feature in future BMW models. But its most memorable features are doors that slide down into pockets in the side sills. Those tall and thick sills provide added structural rigidity that was hard to achieve in convertibles at the time. The Z1 can be driven doorless like a Wrangler or Bronco, but with the added benefit of not having to leave the doors behind.

The showing off stopped under the…

items.title: How Does an F1 Car Get Its Race-Day Livery? Cadillac F1’s Brand Chief Explains
items.summary:
Think about it: a Formula 1 car is arguably the most expensive, fastest-moving art medium on earth. And with just 20 cars on the grid, each 200-mph racer is also one of the most exclusive and expensive billboards in the world. How a team goes about designing its visual identity is complex, yet extremely rewarding work.

In its freshman year in the sport, the Cadillac F1 Team has rolled out four unique liveries to commemorate special races. It started with a cool star-clad design in Miami to celebrate its first race in the U.S., followed by a patriotic and colorful “Stars and Stripes” motif for the British GP (which happened over the 4th of July weekend), an impressive Texas theme for Austin, and lastly, a shimmery “look beneath the surface” one for Vegas. The Texas one is my favorite by far.

Cadillac F1 

I recently caught up with the team’s chief brand advisor, Cassidy Towriss , who’s been intimately involved in crafting the team’s visual persona. From the team kit to the sleek liveries that blitz the tracks, she’s focused on inclusive, fashion-forward designs that look good at the race track and beyond—unlike the usual racing gear, which has historically been sponsor-plastered tees that strictly cater to male race fans.

The haute couture aficionado shared that the creative process behind the team’s O.G. livery, plus designing these one-off looks, comes with a great sense of responsibility, but it’s oh so fun and fulfilling. The biggest challenge is remaining true to the American team’s identity (one of two U.S.-based teams, but the only one that really embraces it),…
items.t: How Does an F1 Car Get Its Race-Day Livery? Cadillac F1’s Brand Chief Explains

items.title: Scout CEO Wants to Ramp Up to 200,000 Units Annually As Quickly as Possible
items.summary:
Scout, the Volkswagen Group brand building modern electric and range-extended off-roaders in the image of the classic International Scout, has done a good job of getting the word out. Now it needs to capitalize on all of the hype it’s generated by converting as many reservations into sales as it prepares to start production of the Traveler SUV and Terra pickup at its new South Carolina factory .

Scout Motors CEO Scott Keogh recently sat down with The Drive for an episode of The Drivecast , and one of the topics discussed was volume. Scout is currently taking $100 refundable fees from customers to reserve a spot in line. These don’t all convert into sales, but Keogh thinks the conversion rate will be high enough to keep the factory humming at or near capacity once production fully ramps up. How quickly that can happen is another matter.

Scout Motors 

Looking at reservation numbers, Keogh is aiming for 400,000 by the time production starts, likely in 2028 . His other goal is selling out 12 to 18 months of production right off the bat. Keogh said the factory can likely build up to 200,000 vehicles annually in its current configuration, so reaching that 400,000-reservation goal would ensure that only half of those reservations would need to be converted into sales to account for a full year’s production capacity. And Keogh is confident Scout can get there.

“I think we will see a high number,” Keogh said on The Drivecast . “The reason I think it’s gonna be high is this isn’t being treated like just the next generation of another car. There’s some people that have literally…

items.title: Liquidating Auto Museum Floods Auction Block With 74 Stellar Cars
items.summary:
It’s easy to be cynical about car museums . Many of them are just a tax dodge for large private collections, as opening them to the public allows the collection to be placed under a tax-free nonprofit organization. But the same is true of fine art, and it accomplishes the same goal of preserving valuable objects that people are passionate about. That is, until the museum goes bust.

Quite a few car museums have shuttered their doors recently, the latest being the Tucson Auto Museum , which shuts down on January 27, 2027. The following day, 74 cars from its collection will be sold off by Kruse Auctions . The lots include some predictable stuff like a 1957 Chevrolet Bel Air, a 1929 Duesenberg Model J Arlington Sedan, and a 1969 Jaguar E-Type coupe. But there’s plenty of weird and wonderful stuff as well.

Credit: Kruse Auctions 

Highlights include Batmobile replicas from both the 1966 television show and the 1992 movie Batman Returns (and what other Batmobiles do you need, really?), plus an entire micro collection of microcars. It covers all the bases with a 1951 Crosley Super Sport Roadster, 1957 Zündapp Janus 250, 1961 Messerschmitt KR200, and 1957 BMW Isetta 300, among others. Kei cars are represented by a 1999 Daihatsu Hijet fire truck and a 1969 Subaru 360. There’s even a Nissan Figaro .

If I was bidding, I’d also take a long look at the hybrid sports car collection. We’re not talking about the second-generation Acura NSX here. In the 1960s and 1970s, a handful of small firms combined Italian coachwork with American powertrains, producing sports cars and grand tourers…
items.t: Liquidating Auto Museum Floods Auction Block With 74 Stellar Cars

items.title: Camaro Owner Claims 35 MPG Out of Small-Block Chevy V8 By Combining Turbo With Motorcycle Carb
items.summary:
The Chevrolet small-block V8 is a versatile engine. It can go in anything from muscle cars to work trucks. But it was never ( and still isn’t ) fuel-efficient. It’s hard to get a big-displacement engine like the ubiquitous 350-cubic-inch (that’s 5.7 liters) to be anything other than a gas guzzler. One tinkerer found a way—and it involves a turbocharger, as well as a motorcycle carburetor.

This is not a case of simply installing an undersized carburetor and tuning the engine to work around it ( although that is also possible ). As detailed in a video from YouTube channel Automotive AZ Rancher , a gentleman named Mike Vannozzi built an entirely new fueling system for his 1978 Chevy Camaro incorporating a Mikuni carburetor normally found on Harley-Davidson engines and a turbo. With it, the 350-powered Camaro gets up to 35 mpg on the highway. That’s better than a 2.0-liter, turbo-four sixth-gen Camaro could manage in EPA testing.

Automotive AZ Rancher via YouTube 

What Vannozzi calls the “turbocharged gasoline vapor system” takes advantage of the fact that gasoline easily vaporizes, turning from a liquid into a gas. He had an epiphany when driving his Dodge Charger around Las Vegas as a teenager in 115-degree heat. When the Charger was low on fuel, popping the fuel filler cap created a hissing noise, the sound of all that vaporized gasoline being released. Vannozzi thought about burning gasoline in this state, a bit like natural gas or propane , building 17 prototypes over three years to perfect the idea. As noted in the video’s comments, many others—including NASCAR legend…
items.t: Camaro Owner Claims 35 MPG Out of Small-Block Chevy V8 By Combining Turbo With Motorcycle Carb
